newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress says open to talks with rulers.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress says open to talks with rulers.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Thursday that it would be willing to negotiate with the United Front coalition even if Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was defeated in a vote of confidence in parliament.

Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told a news conference that the party was prepared to resume talks if the United Front dropped Deve Gowda as its leader. If the alliance did not do so, Congress would vote against the prime minister in the test vote set for Friday, he said.

"Our offer -- that if they change their leader, we are prepared to talk or resume the talks -- still stands," Gadgil said. "If by 11 o'clock tomorrow the matter is not resolved, then we will vote against the government."
Parliament was scheduled to convene to take up the vote of confidence in Deve Gowda at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT) on Friday.
Gadgil said Congress was willing to try to establish a new governing coalition in talks with the United Front even if Deve Gowda lost the vote of confidence.

"Even after government falls, we are prepared to negotiate any arrangement that will contain communal forces," he said, referring to the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which Congress and the United Front accuse of fanning communal tensions by favouring India's Hindu majority.
